thread:
maya: Heads up — after the 6.2 kernel rollout to eu-west2-p this morning, a subset of P4 hosts are hitting repeated PCIe AER resets. nvidia won't finish probe and we get repeated modprobe unload/load loops. Several hosts ended up OOMing or flapping pods. :warning:

maya: dmesg snippets:```
[    8.123456] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: severity=Corrected
[    8.123461] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[    8.123470] nvidia: probe deferred: module dependency or unknown reason
[    9.456789] nvidia: module unloaded, scheduling retry
```

cheng: which kernel exact? 6.2.4-rc1? and which driver?

maya: Kernel image: 6.2.3-rt1 we pushed via kernel-upgrades job at 06:12 UTC. Nvidia driver 525.105.17 (DKMS build) on those hosts. Pattern: p4.* machines with PCIe 3 root complex. Not all hosts affected — ~8/120 in eu-west2-p so far.

liam: Confirmed seeing the same on host p4-34-12. Had to cordon + drain because kubelet was OOMing while trying to restart pods. Autoscaler couldn't replace capacity due to the provisioning backlog.

simone: Any quick mitigation? Can we boot with pci=noaer to silence AER and let driver probe?

maya: Tried pci=noaer as a test — it prevents the flood of AER messages and driver probe completes in my lab run, but it's risky cluster-wide (silences real PCI errors). Also tried modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia which temporarily recovers but then kernel re-triggers AER and it flaps again.

ops-bot: DeployBot: rollback-kernel-6.2 -> queued for eu-west2-p (requires manual approval).

cheng: Two options IMO: 1) pause the 6.2 rollout and roll back affected hosts to 5.15 images, 2) pursue targeted kernel cmdline pci=noaer on those hosts and monitor. Rolling back will take time and churn but is safer. Thoughts?

liam: Rolling back is disruptive but the autoscaler/backlog is already causing customer impact. We should rollback the nodes that are failing and pause the rest of rollout. I'll open a rollback run.

simone: Also file to NVIDIA — logs look like "GPU has fallen off the bus" Xid 79 which they've seen with some PCI enumeration regressions on 6.x. If vendor patch is needed, it might take time. I'll gather sosreport and open NV ticket (NV-18392).

maya: Noted. Immediate actions: 
1) liam to start rolling back the 8 affected hosts to 5.15 images (cordon/drain then redeploy).
2) cheng to hit pause on the rest of eu-west2-p kernel rollout and set rollout to manual.
3) simone to open NV ticket with full dmesg + DKMS build logs.
4) ops to add a temporary alert rule for repeated "AER" + "NVRM" pattern so SRE oncall gets paged if it expands.

liam: Started rollback job for p4-34-12 and p4-34-19. ETA ~12m each because of image pull. Marking nodes DRAIN. :thumbsup:

cheng: Paused rollout and changed canary threshold to 0 in the pipeline, leaving current canary hosts in a safe state.

simone: NV ticket created NV-18392 with logs attached. Vendor suggests reproducer and asked if we can test a 6.1 stable build (they saw repro on 6.2 RC) — we should hold off mass 6.2 until we get vendor confirm.

maya: Cost/ops note: rollback will cause double-scheduling and transient increased bill for eu-west2-p for next 2 hours. Also autoscaler backlog means customers waiting for new ML jobs — ping product/CS if we need to surface outage.

liam: Rollbacks for first 4 hosts finished, all came back healthy on 5.15. Two remaining in flight. No new OOMs after host switch.

maya: Good. Leaving this thread as the coordination record. Follow-ups: update incident ticket, adjust kernel upgrade runbook to include quick pci AER check and vendor contact checklist. :memo:
